result: the groupId filter had to return an empty non-nil device list for a group without devices, otherwise nil would read as 'no restriction'; the device-sim TestReadRepliesCollectsUntilClose flakes on net.Pipe without any relation to this change; PostgreSQL still cannot start under the sandbox, so the new SQL is compiled and asserted as text only

decision: implemented /api/socket on a hand written RFC 6455 server subset and fed it from three existing hooks
why: M3-3 needs push without adding a dependency in a repo that has only pgx and x/crypto, and the sandbox cannot fetch or verify a module; the protocol subset is small because the gateway only ever accepts a socket, never opens one
evidence: go vet ./... and go build ./... clean; go test ./... green; go test -race ./internal/websocket ./internal/api ./internal/alert ./internal/session ./internal/storage/postgres green; 10 websocket tests, 6 socket API tests, one pipeline hook test, one session hook test and one latest positions query test
result: tests cannot bind a TCP port here, so both the websocket package and the socket handler are exercised through net.Pipe with a hijackable ResponseWriter; the token travels in the query string like the Java server, so it lands in access logs; hijacked sockets are not closed by http.Server.Shutdown, and there is no multi-node broadcast or log stream

decision: completed the seven missing processing handlers and wired ProximityRule
why: the chain had three placeholder stages, so time, hemisphere, geolocation, geocoding, engine hours and computed attributes never ran
result: all 15 stages have an implementation; tests pin each handler

decision: added a self contained expression evaluator for computed attributes
why: JEXL is not available in Go and a third party dependency would have to be vendored for one feature
result: arithmetic, comparison, logic, ternary and seven functions supported

decision: added the ten missing REST paths and the password/update alias
why: the official web interface calls them and the previous server answered 404 or 501
result: computed test, accumulators, device image, permissions bulk, TOTP, OpenID, cache, stream and password update are mounted

decision: added TOTP, OpenID Connect and LDAP
why: the Java server supports all three and they were the largest auth gap
evidence: internal/totp RFC 6238 vectors; LDAP net.Pipe tests; OpenID fake transport tests
result: login accepts a TOTP code; directory and provider logins issue the same token

decision: added Redis pub/sub bridging for the live socket feed
why: one node could not show positions another node ingested
evidence: internal/redisbus tests; socket hub remote test
result: the bridge publishes asynchronously so the ingest path never waits for Redis

decision: added deviceInactive, deviceExpiration and events/positions/commands retention
why: the event types existed but nothing produced them and history grew forever
result: inactive events are deduplicated per silence; retention stays off until configured

decision: added seven geocoder and four geolocation providers
why: the provider list was two of twenty four
result: geocoder 9 providers, geolocation 5

decision: added the network (TCP/UDP JSON line) forwarder
why: the Java NetworkForwarder had no Go counterpart
result: AMQP and Kafka remain the only missing transports

decision: added the AMQP 0-9-1 and Kafka producers and selected them with forward.type
why: the gap table listed only AMQP and Kafka, and the sandbox cannot fetch the rabbitmq or kafka Go modules, so both protocols are hand written like MQTT and Redis
evidence: internal/forward amqp and kafka net.Pipe tests, a buildForwarders type test, go test ./... and -race on forward and gateway
result: AMQP declares a durable topic exchange and publishes with publisher confirms; Kafka reads metadata, partitions by device id with murmur2 and produces a v2 record batch with acks=all
